resources.string: A floating Claude Code window over any app. It runs the official Claude Code CLI on this phone with your own Claude subscription — no API key, no Termux.
Fetches the official linux-arm64 build (about 130 MB download, 285 MB on disk) from npm and verifies its checksum.
Sign in with your Claude account
Sign in using the browser, then copy the code it shows and paste it here.
Send a screenshot with each message
Claude runs with permission to use its tools without asking, inside this app\'s private folder. It can\'t read other apps\' data; it only sees your screen through the screenshots you send.
Ask about what\'s on your screen
Each message carries a fresh screenshot, so just ask.
Claude needs you to sign in again.
Other model ID (e.g. a specific version)

Lets Claude Overlay take screenshots for Claude without asking on every start, and — only if you switch on phone control in the overlay — lets Claude tap, swipe, type, draw and open apps on your behalf.

Screenshots without a prompt on every start; needed for Claude to operate apps. Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Claude Overlay. If the switch is greyed out (Android 13+, app installed as APK): App info → ⋮ → \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.
Screenshots come from the accessibility service; no screen-recording prompt needed.
Allow the microphone (to talk to Claude)
The overlay stopped unexpectedly last time
Don\'t let battery saving close the overlay

Lets Claude Overlay keep running in the background. On Samsung also check Settings → Battery → Background usage limits: Claude Overlay must not be in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”, and set its battery use to “Unrestricted”.
Ready – Claude writes with the pen

Android lets apps draw only as a finger, and Samsung Notes then scrolls instead of drawing. The free app Shizuku (no root) lets Claude Overlay write as a real S Pen, with pressure. Shizuku only needs to be started again after the tablet restarts.
Open Shizuku and start it with “Wireless debugging” (follow its pairing steps once), then come back here.
